tools.name: check_dependency
tools.description:
Evaluate a single npm package against the active PkgDiet policy to determine if it is safe, lightweight, and healthy to install. Use this read-only tool before proposing or installing any package. It returns a structured verdict (ALLOW, WARN, BLOCK), health score, cost impact, and supply-chain evidence. A BLOCK is a successful policy decision and must not be bypassed; execution failures are returned as MCP tool errors. It does not install packages, edit files, or modify the project.

Response fields:
- verdict: ALLOW | WARN | BLOCK. Never bypass a BLOCK.
- advisoryVerification.osvChecked: true = OSV security advisory feed confirmed (no CVEs, or CVEs listed in evidence). false = advisory feed was UNREACHABLE — this means CVE status is UNVERIFIED, not safe. Do not treat osvChecked:false as a clean security result.
- advisoryVerification.osvErrorCode: reason the feed was unavailable (timeout, network_error, http_503, etc.) when osvChecked is false.
- advisoryVerification.osvCheckedAt: ISO timestamp of the successful OSV check, or null if the check failed.
- cacheProvenance.fromCache: true if npm metadata came from local cache rather than a live registry fetch.
- cacheProvenance.cachedAt: ISO timestamp when the cached entry was originally fetched.
- cacheProvenance.cacheAgeMs: age of the cache entry in milliseconds.

packageName.description: The exact npm package name to evaluate, such as 'lodash', 'moment', or '@types/node'.

environment.description: The environment context to apply specific policy overrides. Defaults to 'dev'.

tools.name: check_dependencies
tools.description: Evaluate multiple npm packages in a single batch request against the active PkgDiet policy. Use this read-only tool before scaffolding a new project or proposing multiple packages at once. Limit: 50 packages per request. It does not install packages, modify lockfiles, or alter the workspace.

packageNames.description: Array of valid npm package names to evaluate. Limit 50 per request.

environment.description: The target environment to apply specific policy overrides. Defaults to 'dev'.

tools.name: suggest_alternative
tools.description: Suggest a lighter, healthier alternative for an npm package. Use this read-only tool when a developer asks for a package replacement, or when check_dependency returns a WARN or BLOCK verdict (e.g., due to bloat, security risks, or deprecation). It returns a curated list of alternative candidates, including compatibility notes, size guidance, and migration steps. Behavior: It queries the PkgDiet curated alternatives dataset for the given package name and returns ranked recommendations based on the specified runtime and reason. Guidelines: Always verify each recommended candidate with the check_dependency tool before actually installing it or presenting it as a final solution. Do not use this tool to install packages.

packageName.description: The exact npm package name you want to replace (e.g., 'request', 'moment', 'lodash').

reason.description: The primary reason you are seeking an alternative. Helps rank the best candidates (e.g., choose 'size' if replacing a bloated package).

maxResults.description: The maximum number of alternative candidates to return. Recommended: 3.

runtime.description: The target runtime environment where the replacement package will be executed.

includeMigrationNotes.description: If true, includes API compatibility warnings and migration guidance for the suggested alternatives.

tools.name: get_policy
tools.description: Retrieve the active PkgDiet dependency policy constraints for the current workspace. Use this read-only tool when interpreting a WARN or BLOCK verdict, or to understand the project's health and security rules before scaffolding. It does not modify the policy or any project files.

environment.description: The target environment to retrieve the policy for.

tools.name: explain_verdict
tools.description: Retrieve an in-depth explanation of a package verdict, including detailed component health scores, matched policy rules, OSV vulnerability URLs, and evidence justification. Use this tool when an agent or developer needs to explain why a package was WARNED or BLOCKED without hallucinating.

packageName.description: The npm package name to explain (e.g. 'moment', 'request', 'lodash').

environment.description: The target environment to evaluate policy for. Defaults to 'dev'.
